questions.question: The temples at Khajuraho were built during which dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandella dynasty.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Chandella dynasty** ruled in Central India from the **9th to the 13th** century.
 
• The** Khajuraho temples **were built between **950 and 1050 AD** during the reign of the Chandella kings.
 
• The temples are known for their** intricate carvings and sculptures** depicting various deities, animals, and scenes from daily life.
 
• The Khajuraho temples were declared a** UNESCO World Heritage Site** in** 1986.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Gupta dynasty** ruled in India from the **4th to the 6th century.**

 
 
• The Gupta period is known for its achievements in **art, literature, and science.**
 
 
 
• The **Ghazni dynasty** was a **Muslim dynasty** that ruled in **Afghanistan** and parts of India from the 10th to the 12th century.
 
 
• The Ghazni dynasty is known for its** military conquests** and the **plundering of Hindu temples.**
 
 
 
• The** Lodi dynasty** ruled in India from the **15th to the 16th** century.
 
 
• The Lodhi dynasty is known for its** architecture.**

questions.question: Who appoints the Chief Minister of the Union Territory of Delhi?

options.text: Chief Justice of the Supreme Court
Chief Justice of the High Court

questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **President of India.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **President of India **appoints the** Chief Minister of the Union Territory of Delhi, **following the general election results where the majority party or coalition is invited to form the government.
 
• This process is based on the recommendation of the **Lieutenant Governor of Delhi, **who is the **representative of the President in the Union Territory.**
 
• Although the Chief Minister is appointed by the President, the real authority behind the selection lies with the electorate's choice, as the leader of the majority party in the Delhi Legislative Assembly is usually appointed to the position.
 
• The **Chief Minister holds the executive powers in the territory,** albeit under the supervision and with the consent of the Lieutenant Governor and the President of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
 

 **Option**
 **Details**
 
 

 **Option 1**
 The Chief Justice of the Supreme Court is responsible for administering the oath of office to the President of India, not appointing Chief Ministers.
 
 

 **Option 2**
 The Chief Justice of the High Court primarily handles judicial appointments within their jurisdiction and does not appoint Chief Ministers.
 
 

 **Option 4**
 There is no role described as "Neighborhood Governor." Administrative powers in Union Territories are generally exercised by the Lieutenant Governor or the President of India.

questions.question: At which place did Mahatma Buddha give his first 'Dharmachakra Pravartan'?
questions.solution:

• Sarnath is a sacred place of Buddhism, as the Buddha gave his first sermon here after attaining enlightenment at Bodh Gaya.
 
• The event is known in Buddhist texts as dharmachakra-pravartan, the 'turning of the wheel of law'.
 
• At Sarnath, the Buddha also laid the foundation for the sangha or order of monks.
 
• According to Buddhist tradition, he attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya, gave his first sermon at Sarnath, and died in Kushinagar.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• He was born about 2500 years ago(around 563 BC).
 
• He was the son of Suddhodhana and Mahamaya.
 
• He belonged to a small gana known as the Sakya gana and was a Kshatriya.
 
• He was married to Yashodhara.
 
• He learned the technique of meditation from his first teacher Alara Kalama.
 
• He attained enlightenment under a peepal tree at Bodh Gaya in Bihar.
 
• After attaining enlightenment he went to Sarnath, near Varanasi, where he taught for the first time

• He also taught people to be kind and to respect the lives of others, including animals.
 
• He died in 483 BC under a Sal tree in Kushinagar.

questions.question: In India, who among the following is responsible for auditing all receipts and expenditure of the Union and State governments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In India, the** Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)** is responsible for auditing all receipts and expenditure of** the Union and State governments. **
 
• **The CAG** is an independent constitutional authority and is appointed by the** President of India.**
 
• Its primary role is to ensure that the government's financial transactions are conducted in accordance with the laws and regulations in place and that public funds are used efficiently and effectively.
 
• **The CAG submits **its reports to the **President or Governor,** as the case may be, who then lays them before the Parliament or State Legislature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Attorney General for India is the chief legal advisor to the Government of India and is responsible for providing legal advice and guidance to the government on various matters.** The role of the Attorney General includes:

 
 
• **Providing legal advice:** The Attorney General is responsible for providing legal advice and opinions to the Government of India on matters of law and policy. This includes advising on the constitutional validity of laws, treaties, and agreements entered into by the government.
 
• **Representing the government in court: **The Attorney General represents the Government of India in all legal proceedings in the Supreme Court of India and other courts of law. He/she is also responsible for ensuring that the government's legal position is adequately presented and defended in court.
 
• **Initiation of Contempt Proceedings:** The Attorney General has the power to initiate contempt proceedings in the Supreme Court of India against any person who is found to have committed contempt of court.
 
• **Providing legal opinion on references made by the President:** The President of India may refer any legal matter to the Attorney General for his/her opinion, and the Attorney General is required to provide a legal opinion on such references.
 
• **Providing legal opinion on matters referred by the Ministries: **The Ministries of the Government of India may also refer legal matters to the Attorney General for his/her opinion and advice.
 
• **Appointment of Law Officers:** The Attorney General is also responsible for the appointment of the Solicitor General and other law officers of the government.
 
• Overall, the Attorney General for India plays a crucial role in ensuring that the government's legal interests are protected and that the government operates within the framework of the law.
 
 
 
• **The Advocate General **of a State is a Constitutional post and authority duly appointed as per Article 165 of the Constitution of India. The authority and function of Advocate General is also specified in the Constitution of India under Article 165 and 177.
 
• **The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) **is a central government agency responsible for conducting recruitment examinations and selection processes for various **Group A and Group B** posts in the Indian civil services.
 
 
• **Established in 1926, **the UPSC is headquartered in **New Delhi** and is governed by a** chairman and a group of members who are appointed by the President of India.**

questions.question: The Rig Veda is the holiest of the four Vedas, consisting of 10 chapters (called mandalas) of _______ suktas of 10,600 verses.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1028 suktas**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **1028 suktas** are present in the Rig Veda.
 
• The Rig Veda is the holiest of the four Vedas, consisting of 10 chapters (called mandalas).
 
• It contains a total of 10,600 verses.
 
• The Rig Veda is one of the oldest known scriptures in the world and forms the foundation of Vedic literature.
 
• The suktas are hymns dedicated to various deities and natural forces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Rig Veda is divided into ten books, known as Mandalas.
 
• These hymns were composed by various seers (rishis) and were passed down orally through generations before being written down.
 
• The Rig Veda is written in an early form of Sanskrit and is a crucial source of information on early Indo-Aryan civilization.
 
• It includes hymns that are used in various rituals and ceremonies in Hinduism.
 
• The Rig Veda, along with the other three Vedas (Yajur Veda, Sama Veda, and Atharva Veda), forms the core of Vedic literature.
 
• Its hymns cover a wide range of topics, including cosmology, theology, philosophy, and mythology.

questions.question:
Which of the following are the factors that control the Nature and Magnitude of Tides?

1. Uneven distribution of water over the globe

2. Changes in the position of the sun and moon in relation to the earth

3. Irregularities in the configuration of the oceans

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 4.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Tides**

 
• The **periodical rise and fall of the sea level, once or twice a day**, mainly due to the attraction of the sun and the moon, is called a tide.
 
• The moon’s gravitational pull to a great extent and to a lesser extent the sun’s gravitational pull, are the major causes for the occurrence of tides.
 
• Another factor is a centrifugal force which acts opposite to the gravitational pull of the earth.
 
• Tides occur due to a balance between all these forces.
 
• **Factors Controlling the Nature and Magnitude of Tides**
 
 
• The **movement of the moon** in relation to the earth.
 
• **Changes in the position of the sun and moon in relation to the earth. ** *Hence, statement 2 is correct.*
 
• **Uneven distribution of water over the globe. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Irregularities in the configuration of the oceans. ** *Hence, statement 3 is correct.*
 
• On the surface of the earth, the horizontal tide generating forces are more important than the vertical forces in generating the tidal bulges.
 
• The **tidal bulges** on wide continental shelves have greater height. When tidal bulges hit the mid-oceanic islands they become low.
 
• The **shape of bays and estuaries **along a coastline can also magnify the intensity of tides.
 
• Funnel-shaped bays greatly change tidal magnitudes. When the tide is channelled between islands or into bays and estuaries they are called tidal currents (tidal bore is one such tidal current).

questions.question: ________ is an acid in which an atom of the oxygen is connected to an atom of hydrogen and at least one other element.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Oxyacid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Oxyacids** are acids that contain oxygen.
 
• They consist of **hydrogen**, **oxygen**, and at least **one other element**, typically a nonmetal.
 
• The hydrogen atom is **covalently bonded** to an oxygen atom in the molecule.
 
• These acids are important in both organic and inorganic chemistry.
 
• Examples include **sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄)**, **nitric acid (HNO₃)**, and **phosphoric acid (H₃PO₄)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Acid Type
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Oxo Acids**
 Acids that contain hydrogen, oxygen, and at least one other element, where the hydrogen is directly bonded to oxygen.
 
 

 **Hydrohalic Acids**
 Acids that consist of hydrogen and a halogen (e.g., HCl, hydrochloric acid).
 
 

 **Carboxylic Acids**
 Organic acids characterized by the presence of at least one carboxyl group.
 
 

 **Sulfonic Acids**

questions.question: Per capita income for a nation is calculated by dividing the country's national income by its _______.

__
 
• Per capita income is the average income earned per person in a country.
 
• It is calculated by dividing national income by the total population of a country.

 {Per Capita Income} = {National Income over {Population of a country}}

• It includes all individuals of the country not just adults but children and infants also.

questions.question: What is the full form of CNG?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Compressed Natural Gas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Compressed Natural Gas (CNG)** is a fuel that can be used in place of gasoline, diesel fuel, and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).
 
• CNG is made by compressing natural gas (which is mainly composed of methane, CH₄), to less than 1% of the volume it occupies at standard atmospheric pressure.
 
• It is stored and distributed in hard containers at a pressure of 20–25 MPa (2,900–3,600 psi), usually in cylindrical or spherical shapes.
 
• CNG is considered an environmentally friendly alternative because it produces fewer undesirable gases compared to conventional fuels.
 
• The use of CNG can lead to significant reductions in vehicle emissions such as CO₂, NOx, and particulate matter.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Natural Gas Composition**

 
 
• Natural gas is primarily composed of methane (CH₄), but it also contains smaller amounts of other hydrocarbons such as ethane, propane, and butane.
 
• It may also include impurities like water vapor, carbon dioxide (CO₂), nitrogen, and hydrogen sulfide (H₂S).
 
 
 
• **Environmental Benefits**
 
 
• CNG vehicles produce less CO₂ compared to gasoline and diesel vehicles.
 
• They also emit significantly lower levels of NOx and particulate matter, which are major pollutants contributing to urban smog and health issues.
 
 
 
• **Applications of CNG**
 
 
• CNG is used in light-duty passenger vehicles, buses, trucks, and even some locomotives and ships.
 
• It is also used in stationary engines for electricity generation and industrial applications.
 
 
 
• **Safety Considerations**
 
 
• CNG is lighter than air, so it disperses quickly when released, reducing the risk of fire and explosion compared to liquid fuels.
 
• However, CNG storage tanks are built to withstand high pressures and undergo rigorous testing to ensure safety.

questions.question:
Which of the following provision of the Constitution can be amended by a simple majority of the two houses of Parliament.

1. Formation of new states and alteration of areas, boundaries or names of existing states.

2. Directive Principles of State Policy.

3. Abolition or creation of legislative councils in states.

4. Fundamental Rights

Select the correct answer by using the codes given below.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 and 3 only.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

**Types of Amendments:​**

__
 
• **By Simple Majority of Parliament**

 
 
• **A number of provisions in the Constitution can be amended by a simple majority of the two houses of Parliament outside the scope of Article 368. These provisions include:**

 
 
• Admission or establishment of new states.
 
• **Formation of new states and alteration of areas, boundaries or names of existing states.** **Hence, statement 1 is correct.**
 
• **Abolition or creation of legislative councils in states.** **Hence, statement 3 is correct.**
 
• Second Schedule-emoluments,
 
• Allowances, privileges and so on of the president, the governors, the Speakers, judges, etc.
 
• **Quorum in Parliament.**
 
• Salaries and allowances of the members of Parliament.
 
• Rules of procedure in Parliament.
 
• Privileges of the Parliament, its members and its committees.
 
• Use of the English language in Parliament.
 
• A number of puisne judges in the Supreme Court.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **By Special Majority of Parliament**

 
 
• The majority of the provisions in the Constitution need to be amended by a special majority of the Parliament, that is, a majority (that is, more than 50 per cent) of the total membership of each House and a **majority of two-thirds** **of the members of each House present and voting.**
 
• The expression ‘total membership’ means the total number of members comprising the House irrespective of the fact whether there are vacancies or absentees.
 
• The special majority is required only for voting at the third reading stage of the bill but by way of abundant caution, the requirement for the special majority has been provided for in the rules of the Houses in respect of all the effective stages of the bill.
 
• **The provisions which can be amended by this way include (i) Fundamental Rights; (ii) Directive Principles of State Policy; and (iii) All other provisions which are not covered by the first and third categories. Hence, statements 2 and 4 are not correct.**
